_comment: Recurring checks that are not tied to a commit, and so have no natural trigger.
Read by scripts/jobs.py; surfaced at session start (docs/reference/SESSION_START.md).
`next_due` is the earliest `last_run + interval_days` across all jobs, so a session
can decide whether anything needs doing by reading one field instead of reasoning
about every entry. scripts/jobs.py rewrites it; do not maintain it by hand.
`last_run` is state in a tracked file, which is a deliberate trade: the schedule
travels with the repo and is visible to everyone, at the cost of a one-line diff
per run. On a merge conflict, keep the LATER timestamp - it is the one that
A job with no `command` is a human checklist item: jobs.py reports it as due and
records when it was marked done, but runs nothing.

jobs.description: Is a newer openspec release out than the one that generated our skills?
jobs.notes: The only check: there is no CI.

jobs.description: Have the digest-pinned Docker base images moved on their tags?
jobs.notes: The other half of pinning a base image by digest (tests/Dockerfile): the pin keeps builds cacheable across a `docker system prune`, but it also stops security updates arriving implicitly, so the tag has to be watched deliberately. Weekly like openspec-version because it is cheap (one registry HEAD per pin) and the answer changes often. Exit 1 = a pin has moved, 2 = the registry could not be reached, which deliberately does NOT read as current. Bumping is a code change, not bookkeeping: a new base can change system packages, so rebuild the affected image and run its suite. The script finds every `FROM name:tag@sha256:` in the repo, so a second pinned image needs no change here.

jobs.description: cargo audit and npm audit; findings go to docs/BACKLOG.md with severity
jobs.notes: Run `npm audit` at the workspace root (one lockfile covers both UIs) and `cargo audit` in VEN, VTN/bff and lab-core. Before adding an ignore, check whether the advisory reaches code we actually run: the 2026-09-23 pass cleared five findings by dropping rumqttc's default features, because the BFF has no TLS transport at all. Findings go to docs/BACKLOG.md with severity and the reason anything is accepted.

jobs.description: Do the VEN's hexagonal dependency rules still hold, and does the module diagram still describe the code?
jobs.notes: Five dependency rules are scripted (ci/audits/audit_ven_architecture.py) and run automatically; the fifth -- no crate::assets or crate::simulator anywhere in controller/ -- was added 2026-10-03 after two modules had been violating the rule for months in the one directory the first four did not cover. scripts/audit_module_graph.py now also checks that every edge in the Mermaid diagram names a node it defines: the 2026-10-03 pass removed a node and left an edge pointing at it, and Mermaid renders that as a blank box rather than an error. Since R-35 (2026-10-13) the same audit fails when a tasks/ loop (fn spawn*) or a top-level VEN/src directory is missing from the hand-drawn diagram, and when the generated module import graph below it is stale (scripts/gen_module_graph.py rewrites it). Its first run found history_store/, profile/, services/ and spawn_base_load_window missing. What still needs a human pass is whether the hand-drawn nodes' *descriptions* are still true -- the controller ports, boot/, and anything new under infra. The first content check (2026-09-23) found six task loops and the whole fleet-telemetry path behind.

jobs.description: Compare DOCUMENTATION.md and docs/architecture/ against the actual code
jobs.notes: What the first pass (2026-09-23) actually caught, so the next one knows where to look: not broken links but a deleted component described in the present tense — `absorber.rs`, removed twice, still documented as the live deviation mechanism while the arbiter that replaced it went unmentioned. Two cheap sweeps find most of it: (1) extract every file path DOCUMENTATION.md and docs/architecture/ name and check each resolves — remembering that bare names like `reporter.rs` are relative to VEN/src/, so search rather than stat; (2) compare the module tables against `ls VEN/src/controller/` and `VEN/src/tasks/`. docs/history/ is exempt: it is a record, not a description.

jobs.description: Does every sentence in tests/features/ still resolve to exactly one step?
jobs.notes: Per-commit by nature, so the pre-merge gate in .claude/CLAUDE.md is the primary place to run it -- this entry exists because the thing with no natural trigger is checking that MAIN is still clean after someone else's commit, which no session sees. That is not hypothetical: on 2026-10-04 a step declared `{pct:f}` while its feature wrote `at most 2 percent`, and since `parse`'s `f` is fixed-point and needs a decimal point, `2` did not match and the step read as undefined though it was defined four lines away. `tests/entrypoint.sh` aborts the whole suite on any undefined step, so main's entire E2E was blocked for every branch until a run died on it ~20 minutes in. One second here against that. Weekly because it is nearly free. Exit 2 = behave is not installed, which deliberately does NOT read as clean; the container pins behave==1.2.6 while a dev machine may be newer, so this is a pre-filter and the suite's own dry-run stays the authority. House rule it enforces in practice: prefer `{x:g}` over `{x:f}` for numeric step arguments.

jobs.description: Does the full suite still pass on main? Suite selection (ci/suites.map) skips suites a change cannot affect; this finds a wrong skip.
jobs.notes: Hand off a branch equal to main as a full check: `git push -f origin HEAD:ci/full-main && bash ci/ci-handoff.sh --kind check --tiers quick,full`, then `ci/ci-next.sh`. Red here with every merged ticket green means a skip in ci/suites.map was wrong: fix the map rule first, then the failure.
